content.title: Utilities Stewardship Advisory Group
content.summary: The Utilities Stewardship Advisory Group in Arvada is seeking community members to participate in a 2-year term, with the first meeting scheduled for early August 2026. The group will meet three times in 2026 to provide insights and feedback on utility infrastructure, financial planning, and public education regarding water, wastewater, stormwater, and waste hauling services. Applications are due by July 1, 2026, and attendance at an information session is required to apply.
content.body:
Bring your experience to Arvada's commitment to deliver safe, reliable water, wastewater, stormwater, and waste hauling services to our community.

## At a glance

- **Term:** 2 years, with the option to extend
- **Meetings in 2026:**3 meetings, 2 hours each
- **Who can apply:**all Arvada community members
- **First meeting:**early August 2026

[Attend an Info Session](#info)

[Apply by July 1](https://arvada-forms-infrastructure.app.transform.civicplus.com/forms/66178)

## About the group

When you turn on the tap, clean water flows. When you flush, wastewater moves safely to the sewer system. When it rains or snows, stormwater is directed to creeks and ponds. Behind each of these moments is a network of infrastructure, planning, and investment, and funding that pays for it.

Many of these systems were built decades ago and are reaching the end of their useful life and need to be replaced. The City has been planning for and investing in this effort for years (see the [Utilities Transparency webpage](/661) for details). 

The Utility Stewardship Advisory Group brings Arvada community members into this work. **The group helps ensure safe, reliable utility infrastructure while keeping rates at the lowest practical levels through clear, accountable decision-making.**

Members share their experience, provide advisory insight, and strengthen community understanding of how utility systems, including water, wastewater, stormwater, and waste hauling, are funded, operated, and maintained. Members will learn about the trade-offs involved in rate-setting, infrastructure investment, and long-term planning, while also balancing affordability, resilience, and service reliability.

### What you'll gain

- A behind the scenes look at how Arvada plans, funds, and operates the systems that deliver water every day.
- An opportunity to share your perspective on the City’s utility decisions, and a chance to help neighbors understand the City’s utilities and the processes keeping them reliable 24/7, 365 days a year.

## What to expect

In 2026, the group will develop a baseline understanding of the City’s systems, focused on water systems from supply to tap, the rate and fee setting process, and planning for the replacement drinking water treatment plant. In future years, the group will learn more about wastewater, stormwater, and waste hauling services.

The group will meet 3 times in 2026 and 6 times a year in future years. Members should expect to remain committed to the group for 2 years with the opportunity to extend their membership. 

### 2026 meetings

Dates, times, and locations are to be determined based on the responses of selected applicants. Meetings will be 2 hours. The first meeting will be in early August.

### Advisory Group Responsibilities

- Participate in discussions, share perspectives, and offer feedback on financial planning and the goals that the City sets to provide reliable service.
- Consult with the City team in developing the financial framework for infrastructure investments.
- Promote strategies to strengthen public education around public health and utilities services.
- Provide input about utility affordability programs and policies.
- Promote transparency and public understanding of how utility decisions are made and communicated.

## Apply today!

**Applications are due by Wednesday, July 1, 2026.**Applicants will be asked to commit to a 2-year term of service with the opportunity to extend the term. The group is expected to be active through 2030. Accepted members will be asked to review the May 12 and July 28 City Council workshop presentations prior to the first meeting. 

### Information Session

Please join us to learn more about the advisory group, expectations for members, and how to apply. **Attendance at one of the two sessions is required to join the group.** Thank you for being a steward of our utilities and we look forward to meeting you soon!

1. **Virtual: Wednesday, June 24**, 5 - 6:30 p.m., Zoom
   - Email [**[email protected]**](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#9ee9f1ecf5e4f1f0fbdeffece8fffaffb0f1ecf9) to receive a calendar invite and link.
   - Join using this [**Zoom link**](https://arvadaco-gov.zoom.us/j/89227715878?pwd=ckN467ZhfwSvk6L4EtxtJ4sVqNWp2S.1) at the time of the event.
2. **In person: Saturday, June 27**, 10:30 a.m. - 12 p.m., at City Hall, 8101 Ralston Road.

[**RSVP to the information session**](https://forms.gle/8KZCG9oJqqUb7XnC7). RSVP is not required but helpful.

[Apply by July 1](https://arvada-forms-infrastructure.app.transform.civicplus.com/forms/66178)
